sanskrit: yasyāvrātyo vrātyabruvo nāmabibhratī gṛhān atithir āgacchet | karṣed enaṃ na cainaṃ karṣet | etasyai devatāyā udakaṃ yācāmīty asmā udakaṃ yācet | etāṃ devatāṃ pari veveṣmīty enaṃ pari veveṣyāt | etasyām evāsya devatāyāṃ hutam iṣṭaṃ bhavati ya evaṃ veda ||
english: If one who is a non-vrātya bearing the name vrātya comes as a guest to the house — one should draw him in, yet not compel him to stay. One should beg water for him saying "I beg water for this deity"; one should honor him saying "I serve this deity around." For the one who knows thus, whatever oblation or sacrifice is offered is indeed offered to this very deity.

sanskrit: yat prācīṃ diśam anuvyacalad indro bhūtvānu vy acalan mano 'nnādaṃ kṛtvā | manasānnādenānnam atti yaḥ (evaṃ veda) ||
english: When he moved along the eastern direction, having become Indra he moved along, having made mind the food-eater. Whoever knows thus eats food by means of mind as the food-eater.

sanskrit: yad dakṣiṇāṃ diśam anu vyacalan mārutaṃ śardho bhūtvānu vy acalan manyum annādaṃ kṛtvā | manyunānnādenānnam (atti ya evaṃ veda) ||
english: When he moved along the southern direction, having become the host of the Maruts he moved along, having made wrath the food-eater. Whoever knows thus eats food by means of wrath as the food-eater.

sanskrit: yat pratīcīṃ diśam anu vyacalad varuṇo bhūtvānu vy acalad apo 'nnādīḥ kṛtvā | adbhir annādībhir annam (atti ya evaṃ veda) ||
english: When he moved along the western direction, having become Varuṇa he moved along, having made the waters food-eating. Whoever knows thus eats food by means of the waters as food-eaters.

sanskrit: yad udīcīṃ diśam anu vyacalat somo rājā saptaṛṣibhir bhūtvānu vy acalad āhutim annādīṃ kṛtvā | āhutyānnādyānnam (atti ya evaṃ veda) ||
english: When he moved along the northern direction, having become King Soma together with the seven sages he moved along, having made the oblation food-eating. Whoever knows thus eats food by means of the oblation as food-eating.

sanskrit: yad dhruvāṃ diśam anuvyacalad viṣṇur bhūtvānu vy acalad virājam annādīṃ kṛtvā | virājānnādyānnaṃ (atti ya evaṃ veda) ||
english: When he moved along the fixed direction (the zenith or nadir), having become Viṣṇu he moved along, having made the Virāj food-eating. Whoever knows thus eats food by means of the Virāj as food-eating.

sanskrit: yad ūrdhvaṃ diśam anu vyacalad bṛhaspatir bhūtvānu vy acalad vaṣaṭkāram annādaṃ kṛtvā | vaṣaṭkāreṇānnādenānnaṃ (atti ya evaṃ veda) ||
english: When he moved along the upward direction, having become Bṛhaspati he moved along, having made the vaṣaṭ-call the food-eater. Whoever knows thus eats food by means of the vaṣaṭ-call as the food-eater.

sanskrit: yat paśūn anuvyacalad rudro bhūtvānu vy acalad oṣadhīr annādīḥ kṛtvā | oṣadhībhir annādībhir annaṃ (atti ya evaṃ veda) ||
english: When he moved along the cattle, having become Rudra he moved along, having made the plants food-eating. Whoever knows thus eats food by means of the plants as food-eaters.

sanskrit: yad devān anuvyacalad īśāno bhūtvānu vy acalad balam annādaṃ kṛtvā | balenānnādenānnaṃ (atti ya evaṃ veda) ||
english: When he moved along the gods, having become Īśāna (the lord) he moved along, having made strength the food-eater. Whoever knows thus eats food by means of strength as the food-eater.

sanskrit: yan manuṣyān anuvyacalad agnir bhūtvānu vy acalat svāhākāram annādaṃ kṛtvā | svāhākāreṇānnādena (annam atti ya evaṃ veda) ||
english: When he moved along humankind, having become Agni he moved along, having made the svāhā-call the food-eater. Whoever knows thus eats food by means of the svāhā-call as the food-eater.

sanskrit: yat pitṝn anuvyacalad yamo bhūtvānu vy acalat svadhākāram annādaṃ kṛtvā | svadhākāreṇānnādena (annam atti ya evaṃ veda) ||
english: When he moved along the ancestors (pitṛs), having become Yama he moved along, having made the svadhā-call the food-eater. Whoever knows thus eats food by means of the svadhā-call as the food-eater.

sanskrit: yat prajā anuvyacalat prajāpatir bhūtvānu vy acalat prāṇam annādaṃ kṛtvā | prāṇenānnādena (annam atti ya evaṃ veda) ||
english: When he moved along creatures (prajā), having become Prajāpati he moved along, having made the breath (prāṇa) the food-eater. Whoever knows thus eats food by means of breath as the food-eater.

sanskrit: yad antardeśān anuvyacalad vāyur bhūtvānu vy acalad vātam annādaṃ kṛtvā | vātenānnādena (annam atti ya evaṃ veda) ||
english: When he moved along the intermediate regions, having become Vāyu he moved along, having made the wind (vāta) the food-eater. Whoever knows thus eats food by means of wind as the food-eater.

sanskrit: yad diśo 'nuvyacalat parameṣṭhī bhūtvānu vy acalad brahmānnādaṃ kṛtvā | brahmaṇānnādenānnam atti ya evaṃ veda ||
english: When he moved along the directions, having become Parameṣṭhin he moved along, having made brahman the food-eater. Whoever knows thus eats food by means of brahman as the food-eater.

sanskrit: tasya sapta prāṇāḥ saptāpānāḥ sapta vyānāḥ | yo 'sya prathamaḥ prāṇa ūrdhvo nāma so 'yam agniḥ | yo 'sya dvitīyaḥ prāṇaḥ proḍho nāma so 'sāv ādityaḥ | yo 'sya tṛtīyaḥ prāṇo 'bhyūḍho nāma so 'sau candramāḥ | yo 'sya caturthaḥ prāṇo vibhūr nāma so 'yaṃ pavamānaḥ | yo 'sya pañcamaḥ prāṇo 'parimito nāma ta ime paśavaḥ | yo 'sya ṣaṣṭhaḥ prāṇaḥ priyo nāma tā imāḥ prajāḥ | yo 'sya saptamaḥ prāṇo yonir nāma tā imā āpaḥ ||
english: He has seven prāṇas (in-breaths), seven apānas (out-breaths), seven vyānas (diffused breaths). His first prāṇa is named Ūrdhva (the upward) — that is this Agni (fire). His second prāṇa is named Proḍha (the advanced) — that is yonder Āditya (sun). His third prāṇa is named Abhyūḍha (the borne-up) — that is yonder Candramā (moon). His fourth prāṇa is named Vibhū (the pervading) — that is this Pavamāna (purifying wind). His fifth prāṇa is named Aparimita (the immeasurable) — those are these cattle. His sixth prāṇa is named Priya (the beloved) — those are these creatures (prajāḥ). His seventh prāṇa is named Yoni (the womb/source) — those are these waters.
